But X know that his colleague the Minister of Marine and Fisheries (Hon. Mr. Prd-fontaine) has gone several times-in view, I suppose, of the fact that he thought he would lie entrusted with carrying out these works. But I have only to say that I am surprised that the work is not to be completed by the time it was understood that it would be completed when 1 left office.

We have had a most interesting discussion on the subject of dredges and dredging. There has been a considerable conflict of opinion on the question whether this work ought to be carried out with dredges under the control of the government or let out to contractors. It seems to me that an important element in the consideration of the question is to know how soon the dredges can be got ready. We have been told by the exMinister of Public Works (Hon. Mr. Tarte) that when he came into office in 1896 there were practically no dredges at all, and that it has been necessary, in the time that has since elapsed, to equip the department in this respect. It seems to me that it was a very fair question to ask when the dredge was begun, and it is only proper that when a question of that sort is put, that we should have an answer that we can rely upon. I put the question to the minister in whose department the work is being done and who ought to be able to give the information. After consulting his officials on the floor, he told me that the work was begun two years ago and that it will take another year before it is finished. Is that correct or not ? For the ex-Minister of Public Works says it is not. The House ought to be enlightened on that point.

Let us discuss it.
The MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS, t My hon. friend the ex-Minister of Public Works (Hon. Mr. Tarte) must know that when I make a statement wflth regard to matters that have taken place in the department, I make it on the authority of the officials of the department and not from my own knowledge. I remember very well the hon. gentleman's statements in the House and out of it to myself privately. We were all anxious that the work should be proceeded with, as the hon. gentleman's idea was that the work could be carried on more quickly at Sorel than it has actually been carried on. I felt anxious about it because I knew that the dredge was urgently required. After examination I do find that there is a difference of opinion between the officials of the department and my hon.
friend as to when it may be completed. If everything goes well, we expect it will be ready at the beginning of next year. The first vote-
The first vote I know all about.

I can only speak from the information I find in the records of the department. I think the hon. gentleman will admit that there is no official of the department who would willingly make a wrong statement with regard to the business of the department. I found that the first vote was in 1901-2. The work in one sense was not commenced then, though it was fully in hand. The material was purchased, goods were purchased, and the work has been going on more or less ever since. Up to the present time there has been expended $285,000 on this work.

I want to explain further in regard to that work. The Minister of Justice seems to be anxious to know aH about it. The first time an amount of money was placed in the estimates was in 1901-2. Everybody knows that after an item is voted in the House, the work does not start immediately. Parliament is prorogued, and then preparations are made to go on with the work. The money was placed in the estimates, but that was not the beginning of the work. I instructed Mr. Robinson, after a certain time, to prepare plans, and that took a good deal of time. Practically the work has been going on for over one year. Now I do not wish to leave the committee under the impression that I blame the Minister of Public Works for the delay. Nothing of the kind. I know he has done everything he could, and I am only sorry that the dredge is not completed.

As I understand the exMinister of Public Works, he complains that possibly the distribution of patronage in a different way is causing the delay. Is there any information to be given to the committee on that subject ? This is a serious matter. This dredge is going to be a valuable addition to the force, and is going to cost a large sum of money. The hon. gentleman, before leaving office, I understand, had purchased the greater part of the material for the construction of the dredge, and he makes the suggestion tonight that possibly- the method of administering the patronage of the department is causing delay. Is there any change in the method ?

I am unable to answer that question with regard to time. The first vote was taken in 1901, the second in 1902, the next in 1903. This is the fourth vote that is being asked for in connection with this work. I may

say that no change has been made that 1 am aware of in regard to this work.

The ex-Minister of Public Works appears to be speaking of something that he knows pretty well when he says definitely that there is a question of patronage that enters into this matter, and prevents the rapid completion of the work. He suggests what has not been answered by the Minister of Public Works, that by reason of the Minister of Marine and Fisheries having in contemplation to carry out that which he had announced upon a public platform, and to secure for himself enlarged powers and patronage, is himself delaying the matter in order that he may secure that larger control of public works, and obtain possession of that larger patronage. I think we should have some explicit statement by the present Minister of Public Works that this difficulty which seems to have arisen will in some way be averted.
What difficulty does the hon. gentleman refer to 7

I will explain more fully. I say that he should assure us .that this difficulty shall not continue to stand in the way of carrying out this work. I repeat that it appears that the present Minister of Marine and Fisheries has promised in the province of Quebec that he is to have a larger share of public works.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
speechtext: I call the hon. member to order. The question of the statement of the Minister of Marine and Fisheries in regard to the division of the duties of the two departments has been ruled out of order.
No, only as to one item.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
speechtext: If it is not relevant to one item, you cannot raise it on another item.

I draw the attention of the Chairman to this fact, that we are endeavouring to get information as to the cause of the delay in finishing this dredge, and it .is in connection with that item for the dredge that we are discussing the statements of the Minister of Marine and Fisheries.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
speechtext:
I am now ruling on the position taken by the hon. member for Simeoe (Mr. Lennox), who was going on to discuss the question of the division of the duties pertaining to the Minister of Public Works and the Minister of Marine and Fisheries, a question that had been under discussion the whole evening on another item. Now this is what Bourinot says :
It is irregular to discuss any matters in committee which are not relevant to the resolution
under consideration.
Now I do not see any relevancy between the statements made by the Minister of Marine and Fisheries as to the future intentions of the government to make a division of the duties pertaining to these departments, and the item in the estimates which is before the committee.

I think, Mr. Chairman, you misunderstood the matter which has been brought up. I do not think the hon. Minister of Public Works has the slightest objection to giving the information. The question is simply as to whether the money is to be expended by the Department of Public Works, or by some other department. It is absolutely relevant and it is not exactly the question which you have been settling.

G?he hon. gentleman was not in when I made that statement before, and I am sure if he had been he would have been perfectly satisfied. As to any change of patronage, or any change in the officials, I have stated most' distinctly that there has been none at all. There has been no interference in any way and no change that I am aware of. If there is anything more in this regard upon which he wants information, I have not the slightest idea what he is hinting at.

Mr. Chairman, I am quite willing to submit to your ruling in the matter. It is not very material to my purpose in dealing with the question that I have to deal with whether I shall pursue exactly the same lines that I was pursuing or not. But I was asked a question by the hon. Minister of Public Works and I propose to answer it, and I hope, that I shall have the hon. Minister of Public Works copying my example and answering the question explicitly and definitely. What I submit is this : We have had a statement by the ex-Minister of Public Works (Hon. Mr. Tarte) that the difficulty which has arisen and which has caused the delay has been the question of patronage. We have had it further stated by the ex-Minister of Public Works that it has arisen in connection with the question as to what power shall be exercised hereafter by the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries. I ask the hon. Minister of Public Works to state whether that state of things exists or not. If it does exist, why then, it is a very serious difficulty and one that should be developed by this committee and one that should be a- reason for not passing this item.
I will answer in the hon. gentleman's own language and say that it does not exist. I hope that is clear.
We, of course, understand in regard to all the other items the assurance which the hon. minister has 1 already given equally applies ?

Yes.
New dredging plant-Ontario and Quebec, $75,000.

I am asking for this amount of money that we may be able to provide a new dredge for the important work that is necessary to be done below Quebec. I know that it will take some time to build this dredge. If it is possible to purchase a dredge, as I have been ready to do, I would be very glad to do it. But we cannot commence, I think, too soon to appropriate some money for the purpose of building a new dredge. I am informed by the chief engineer that a dredge suitable for the work can be built for $75,000.

Is that a dipper dredge ?
' The MINISTER OF PUBLIC WORKS.
Yes.
If I understand the hon. minister, this dredge is going to be used below Quebec ?
Yes.
It is a dipper dredge 1
Yes.
Must we understand that this is to dredge the channel opposite Crane island, for instance ?
No. This is for dredging at various points along the river and harbours and at the approaches to wharfs.
That dredge will not be called upon to work in deep water ?
It will not be used for channel work. It would not be suitable for that.
Is that dredge to be built to dredge, for instance, the approaches to wharfs ?
Yes, for instance, we have an application from Murray Bay.
Is it going to be a steel dredge ?
Yes.
What will be its capacity ?
Between 2,000 yards and 2,500 yards.
Where is that dredge going to be built ?

If we could have it built at the govern-Mr. BORDEN (Halifax).
ment shops it is the intention to do so. There is such an urgent demand that if we could purchase a dredge we would be glad to do it, so as to be able to do the work during the present year. If not we will have to build a dredge.
About what capacity of dipper is used on a dredge of that size ?
The chief engineer informs me that it will be a three or four yard dipper.
Of course, there is some difference between buying a dredge and building one. I think the committee ought to know whether the hon. minister intends to buy a dredge or build one.

I do not think there is a very material difference. There is a lot of work that we must do. It has been represented to me that we might possibly buy a dredge. I do not know of any dredge for sale at the present time; in fact, from the inquiries the department has been making, I do not believe there is one in the Dominion of Canada to-day suitable for the work that can be bought. If we could buy a suitable dredge, I think it would be the best policy to buy one. But we are taking the vote for the purpose of procuring a dredge and from my information there is not one which could be bought and we may have to build one.
What are the dimensions of the dredge going to be ?
I have not the dimensions or plans prepared yet. I am asking for this vote for the purpose of procuring a dredge or building one.

I would like to ask the hon. minister a question in connection with the item we have just passed which I did not have the opportunity of asking at the time. What will the other dredge cost to complete and what will be the cost of this dredge that we are now discussing ?

The large dredge is estimated to cost $520,000, and the chief engineer informs me that according to the plans and specifications which he proposes to draw for this one, it cam be completed for $75,000.
New dredging plant, Manitoba-self propelling snag-boat to work in Red and Assinlboiue rivers, $10,000.
Do you purpose building that in Manitoba ?

I would like the lion. Minister of Public Works to explain this item and to state whether there is any probability of having that boat built this year ? This is a revote. This boat has been needed

badly on those rivers for some time. The item, I believe, has had a great deal of consideration. I would ask if there is any probability of having the boat built this year ?

I find that this amount has been voted for some three or four sessions, and on Inquiry from the engineers I find that no action has been taken. I have asked for a further report as to what work is to be done and as to the necessity for this snag-boat. Until I get that information from the resident engineer, I could not pledge myself to spend this money, although we are asking for it.
I see that the item just passed of $75,000 is for Ontario and Quebec. Is there anything for Ontario in that ?
We will have the new dredge for Ontario ready in four or five weeks. It has been customary to take this vote in this way.

It was almost impossible to get material or labour for this class of work in the west last year. As a matter of fact, I believe it will require 25 or 30 per cent more to build the same kind of a snag-boat this year, because material and labour have advanced, and I think the resident engineer will ask for $12,500 more in the supplementaries.
Where do the snags come from ?
You will strike one soon.

The Red River and the boundary line of Lake Winnipeg is filled with trees and snags and one thing or another, and vessels drawing two or three feet of water cannot pass along that river at low water until it is cleared.
New dredging plant generally, $60,000.
What is the meaning of this ?

This is for the construction of new plant to meet the exigencies of the government dredging service. I may say that these applications have been sent in as urgent in regard to the dredges in the various provinces. It covers new barges and tugs, &e. I may say that if all these applications were granted they would amount to over $300,000, but the chief engineer after going over them thinks he could do with a vote of $60,000 to keep the plant in work-.ing order.
Is this for new plant or repairing ?
Practically for new plant.
Where will these be built ?
They will be purchased by contract.
How many shops has the government for the construction of dredges?
We have only one shop at Sorel.
How is it possible to construct this new $75,000 dredge when the $500,000 dredge will not be built until next year.'

That large dredge will be out of the way and the other work will be going on. I have had little opportunity of looking into the shop at Sorel, but the Information I have received from the engineer of the department is that for repairing and building such a dredge as this, and tugs and scows, we can do that cheaper than by , going to the other shops. As to doing this very large and important work where we have to purchase considerable machinery, I am not prepared to say at the present time.
How will the minister provide for this new plant ?
We will advertise for tenders.
Every shipyard will have an opportunity to supply them?

Yes.
Dredging-Quebec and Ontario, $75,000.
Where is this money to be spent
This vote is taken for the maintenance of the government dredges. There is one at Kingston, and my intention is to send one to Port Hope and one to Gananoque, and to different parts of the province.
We should have a statement ns to how many places the work will be done in.
I cannot remember all the places now, but, if my hon. friend is agreeable, I will bring down the programme and lay it on the Table.
Very well.
Will the minister also bring down the information I asked for, as to the different counties in which these dredges were at work last summer.

I can give my hon. friend that information now. The ' Challenge ' was at Kincardine, Midland, Owen Sound and Collingwood. The ' Ontario ' at Port Stanley, Rondeau and Kingsville. The ' Nipissing ' at Burlington Piers, Bronte, Hamilton, Port Hope

and Bowmanville. The ' Queen ' at Osha-wa, Bowmanville, Dunbarton and Pickering. The 'Sir Richard ' at Hawkesbury, Grenville, Bath and Adolphustown.
Some resolutions reported.
On motion of the Minister of Finance, House adjourned at 12.25 a.in., Friday.

Friday, May 8, 1903.
